text:
alex: Quick heads-up — after last night's spike I sketched a short plan for graceful degradation of dashboard rendering when the query layer is overloaded. posting it here for quick feedback. https://go/repro-dash-render

maria: nice. can you paste the short flow here?

alex: sure. tl;dr: swap from live query fanout -> render -> ui to a tiered fallback: 1) live queries (normal), 2) cached projection tiles (fast), 3) static snapshot (stale) + background revalidate. also move minimal RBAC checks earlier so we can serve cached tiles without hitting full auth graph every time.

ben: moving RBAC earlier sounds risky. if we shortcut checks to serve cached tiles we need to ensure the cache key includes an auth fingerprint. otherwise we leak.

alex: agreed. plan is to compute a small auth fingerprint (tenant_id + role-set-hash) and use it as part of tile cache key. no full policy eval in fast path.

liyah: that fingerprint idea is good. does it cover attribute-based policies? e.g., project-level flags?

alex: attributes that change often are still validated in the slow path. fast path only for stable, coarse-grained perms. we'll mark some panels as "auth-sensitive" and they won't be cacheable.

tim: how will this affect SLOs and budgets? need numbers to show cost/latency win + risk.

alex: rough numbers: serving from projection tiles cuts median render latency from ~240ms to ~60ms, p95 from 900ms to 250ms. reduces fanout load by ~3x. snapshots are ~20ms but stale.

ben: ok, with auth fingerprint + marking sensitive panels we avoid leaks. but cache invalidation is the hard part. dashboards change layout or datasource; eviction chatter could thump the query layer.

maria: could we use a small service that subscribes to model config changes and issues selective invalidation? keep invalidation coarse (panel-level) and debounce.

alex: exactly. proposal: projection-sync service watches definitions and emits invalidation events. use debounce window 5s, per-tenant per-dashboard tombstone. this keeps invalidation QPS low.

liyah: what about partial degradation on overload? e.g., some panels degrade to tiles while others stay live. need UI contract for per-panel placeholders and loading states.

alex: UI contract: panels can be in states: live, cached-tile, snapshot, error. client shows watermark "stale" for cached/snapshot and allows refresh. we'll add a tiny UX pattern to reduce confusion.

ben: operational concerns: telemetry must include path tag (live|tile|snapshot) and auth-fingerprint hit/miss. also add a metric for "degraded-by-cpu" to correlate with node pressure.

infra-bot: deploy: projection-sync v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-19T09:14:10Z :rocket:

alex: spike tasks I'm proposing:
- implement auth-fingerprint lib (server + small client helper)
- projection-sync service (watch definitions, emit invalidations)
- renderer: add fast-path reading from tile cache + fallback logic
- console-ui: per-panel fallback UI and telemetry tags
- perf tests + chaos (overload query layer and ensure graceful degradation)

maria: + make a short RFC for the safety boundaries: what is allowed in fast-path vs slow-path. we need sign-off from security for the fingerprint tradeoff.

tim: product ask: ensure snapshot path includes a freshness timestamp and a link to request a manual refresh. also consider a toggle for admins to always force live queries.

ben: one more thought — long-term we should decouple projection computation from render so we can scale them independently. consider a projection worker fleet with explicit backpressure signals to renderer.

alex: yes long-term refactor: split renderer into renderer-controller (orchestrates fallbacks + auth fingerprint) and tile-store/projection workers. low-risk spike will implement the fast-path on top of current renderer first.

liyah: can I take the UI piece? I can prototype panel states and the watermark by EOW.

alex: awesome. ben can you own telemetry + perf tests? maria will draft RFC, tim will vet product UX. I'll take the projection-sync and auth-fingerprint spike.

maria: assign a short JIRA? we should at least track the spike and the RFC separately.

alex: created JIRA INF-3217 and RFC-2026-dash-degrade. links in thread: https://jira/repo/INF-3217 https://go/rfc-dash-degrade

ben: quick config snippet suggestion for the renderer fallback thresholds:

```
fallback:
  max_live_latency_ms: 700
  prefer_tile_under_load: true
  tile_stale_ttl_sec: 60
```

alex: perfect. we'll iterate. thanks for quick replies. planning a short sync tomorrow to align on spikes. :thumbsup:

tim: thanks — this looks pragmatic and measurable.

infra-bot: calendar: "Dash degrade spike sync" scheduled 2026-03-20 11:00 UTC (invite sent).

alex: closing thread for now, will post RFC link when ready.
